snapshot.text: P PlaiceToMeat 426 Birmingham Road, Wylde Green Sign out All playbooks PLAYBOOK Butcher words explained A plain-words guide to the butchery and shop terms you'll see around the app. No prior experience needed. WHY IT MATTERS The app uses a few trade words. Knowing what they mean — especially yield and margin — lets you make confident decisions instead of guessing. Step by step 1 Carcass — a whole animal after slaughter, before it's cut up. You buy these and break them into cuts. 2 Cut (or joint) — a piece of meat ready to sell, like a leg, shoulder or chops. 3 Yield — how much saleable meat you actually get from a carcass after bone, fat and trim come off. More yield means more to sell. 4 Trim — the fat, sinew and offcuts removed while preparing a cut. Usually goes to mince or waste. 5 Bone-in / boneless — whether a cut still has its bone. Boneless weighs less but is often easier to sell. 6 Batch — one delivery or carcass recorded in the shop, with its own weight, cost and use-by date. 7 Cost per kg — what the meat costs you to buy, per kilo. The app needs this to work out your profit. 8 Margin — the profit left after costs, shown as a share of the price. A bigger margin is a healthier line. 9 Days of cover — how many days your current stock will last at the rate it's selling. 10 Cutting guide / cut sheet — the plan for how a carcass breaks into cuts, with expected weights and suggested prices. 11 Use-by (expiry) — the date meat must be sold or used by. After it, treat it as waste. 12 Halal certificate — a supplier's proof their meat is halal. It must be kept in date. Watch out for You don't need to memorise these — come back whenever a word on screen is unfamiliar. The two that drive your profit most are yield and margin. Get comfortable with those first.

snapshot.text: P PlaiceToMeat 426 Birmingham Road, Wylde Green Counter Food safety Today Shop detail Shop view Olivia Owner Sign out All playbooks PLAYBOOK Butcher words explained A plain-words guide to the butchery and shop terms you'll see around the app. No prior experience needed. WHY IT MATTERS The app uses a few trade words. Knowing what they mean — especially yield and margin — lets you make confident decisions instead of guessing. Step by step 1 Carcass — a whole animal after slaughter, before it's cut up. You buy these and break them into cuts. 2 Cut (or joint) — a piece of meat ready to sell, like a leg, shoulder or chops. 3 Yield — how much saleable meat you actually get from a carcass after bone, fat and trim come off. More yield means more to sell. 4 Trim — the fat, sinew and offcuts removed while preparing a cut. Usually goes to mince or waste. 5 Bone-in / boneless — whether a cut still has its bone. Boneless weighs less but is often easier to sell. 6 Batch — one delivery or carcass recorded in the shop, with its own weight, cost and use-by date. 7 Cost per kg — what the meat costs you to buy, per kilo. The app needs this to work out your profit. 8 Margin — the profit left after costs, shown as a share of the price. A bigger margin is a healthier line. 9 Days of cover — how many days your current stock will last at the rate it's selling. 10 Cutting guide / cut sheet — the plan for how a carcass breaks into cuts, with expected weights and suggested prices. 11 Use-by (expiry) — the date meat must be sold or used by. After it, treat it as waste. 12 Halal certificate — a supplier's proof their meat is halal. It must be kept in date. Watch out for You don't need to memorise these — come back whenever a word on screen is unfamiliar. The two that drive your profit most are yield and margin. Get comfortable with those first.

snapshot.text: P PlaiceToMeat 426 Birmingham Road, Wylde Green Counter Food safety Today Shop detail Shop view Olivia Owner Sign out All playbooks PLAYBOOK Butcher words explained A plain-words guide to the butchery and shop terms you'll see around the app. No prior experience needed. WHY IT MATTERS The app uses a few trade words. Knowing what they mean — especially yield and margin — lets you make confident decisions instead of guessing. Step by step 1 Carcass — a whole animal after slaughter, before it's cut up. You buy these and break them into cuts. 2 Cut (or joint) — a piece of meat ready to sell, like a leg, shoulder or chops. 3 Yield — how much saleable meat you actually get from a carcass after bone, fat and trim come off. More yield means more to sell. 4 Trim — the fat, sinew and offcuts removed while preparing a cut. Usually goes to mince or waste. 5 Bone-in / boneless — whether a cut still has its bone. Boneless weighs less but is often easier to sell. 6 Batch — one delivery or carcass recorded in the shop, with its own weight, cost and use-by date. 7 Cost per kg — what the meat costs you to buy, per kilo. The app needs this to work out your profit. 8 Margin — the profit left after costs, shown as a share of the price. A bigger margin is a healthier line. 9 Days of cover — how many days your current stock will last at the rate it's selling. 10 Cutting guide / cut sheet — the plan for how a carcass breaks into cuts, with expected weights and suggested prices. 11 Use-by (expiry) — the date meat must be sold or used by. After it, treat it as waste. 12 Halal certificate — a supplier's proof their meat is halal. It must be kept in date. Watch out for You don't need to memorise these — come back whenever a word on screen is unfamiliar. The two that drive your profit most are yield and margin. Get comfortable with those first.
